policy: Every waiver carries RUSTSEC ids (or an explicit non-advisory reason), a granted date, an expiry as an absolute date AND a minor-version bound (whichever comes first), a replacement trigger, an owner and evidence. An expired waiver is a FAILURE, not a warning (ADR-0031 condition 4; same shape as kernel/01 K-04's expiring difference register).

subject: rustybuzz@0.20.1
ttf-parser@0.25.1
waivers.why: DC-17 / kernel/03 K-05 name rustybuzz as the only OpenType shaping engine. Both crates are unmaintained (RUSTSEC) with no safe upgrade, and neither has a known vulnerability. The alternative (skrifa plus a maintained shaper) changes DC-17 and needs its own ADR.
waivers.replacement_trigger: any RUSTSEC vulnerability (not merely unmaintained) against rustybuzz or ttf-parser; OR skrifa plus a maintained shaper that satisfies the DC-17 feature set without a C dependency; OR two minor releases of TermAI, whichever comes first
